parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of trans identity and no sodomy law, with a functioning federal hate-crime statute and courts that have enjoined several executive orders — so this is not a 0.0–0.2 jurisdiction. But the combined regime carries traveller-facing tier-1 exposures: federal single-sex facility exclusion by birth sex in government-funded buildings, border refusal where documents or records cast doubt on sex (with reported passport confiscation, stranding and lifetime fraud-ineligibility risk), and immigration custody where trans detainees report forced labour, beatings and sexual abuse. The division adds a licence/birth-certificate marker ban, a minor care ban, and a pending campus/prison bathroom bill. Remedies are partial and do not reach facilities or custody, so the exposures subtract into High Risk.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal rules bar self-selected markers on new passports/visas; officers instructed to refuse where documents or records cast doubt on sex, with possible lifetime fraud ineligibility; travellers report confiscated passports and stranding; foreign governments issued advisories and detentions of regional citizens occurred.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports valid until expiry; misrepresentation finding is never automatic and requires four elements with limited waivers; policy under active litigation; legal-aid FAQ exists.
entry_documents.interaction: A marker/presentation discrepancy at a port of entry can escalate from secondary inspection to refusal, then into immigration detention or removal.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody: trans men reported forced labour justified by gender, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse; the corrections bureau adopted conversion-style policies (hair cutting, hormone removal) and stopped reporting trans prisoner numbers.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. The prior executive order on LGBTQ prisoners was rescinded and no operative safeguard for trans detainees is recorded.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Border refusal or a fraud allegation feeds directly into the immigration-detention system described above.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity, reaching federal buildings and federally funded settings; a state bill would extend birth-sex facility rules to public schools, universities and prisons, and passed the upper chamber.
federal_state_facilities.protection: The division currently imposes no restroom restriction; two cities protect restroom use by ordinance; a 2023 appellate injunction barred one school's restriction.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal facility rules apply irrespective of the division's more permissive local law, so local tolerance does not neutralise the operative exclusion.

care_services.exposure: State law bans gender-transition surgery, blockers and hormones for anyone under 18, in force since February 2024; federal orders frame minor care as mutilation and target funding.
care_services.protection: Adult care availability is not documented either way. No documented denial of emergency care to trans visitors.
care_services.interaction: A trans minor travelling with a guardian cannot obtain such care in this division, and clinicians face legal exposure for providing it.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: The 2026 federal counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' violent groups; a DOJ reward memo invokes 'radical gender ideology'; an order directs investigation and prosecution of teachers who use a trans minor's preferred name or pronouns.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The strategy states counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; several related orders have been blocked or enjoined; no prosecution of a trans visitor is documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Framing raises discovery risk around visible advocacy or a family's social support of a trans minor, though the documented target class is organisations described as violent.

minors_guardians.exposure: Minor care ban; school policy requiring written parental notice when a minor requests a different name or pronoun; a bathroom bill covering schools; federal prosecution framing of teachers who affirm a minor.
minors_guardians.protection: A 2023 appellate injunction barred one school from restricting a trans student's restroom use during litigation; some municipal ordinances protect restroom use.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian travelling with a trans minor meets outing risk in sex-segregated facilities plus a hostile legal framing of the guardian's own support.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence against visitors is documented in the dossier; travel guidance merely advises checking recent violence reports. Advisories from allied governments exist.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Federal hate-crime statute covers gender identity; the division's 2019 law makes gender-identity bias an aggravating circumstance. Enforcement data is not recorded.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Recourse exists on paper, but its operation for a trans visitor is undocumented, so it cannot be credited as working protection.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Courts and agencies are themselves enforcing hostile rules — the passport-marker policy took effect after Supreme Court action, and the division's motor-vehicle marker ban is being implemented administratively.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Litigation has enjoined several executive orders and challenges the marker ban and passport policy; a civil-liberties suit is pending.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are slow, partial and do not reach facility exclusion or custody practice; where institutions enforce the hostile rule, functioning courts aggravate rather than mitigate.

anchor_checks.comparison: That anchor has coercive custody, extortion, guards mocking presentation and a coerced statement — serious, but no state-level structural exclusion. This dossier lacks the extortion pattern but exceeds it: lawful federal facility exclusion, entry refusal with stranding, and documented immigration-custody abuse are institutional, not improvisational, so it rates slightly above.

Similar border-discrepancy denial of entry and invasive review, but that anchor expressly bars detention and only denies entry. Here detention for document issues is reported, custody harm is documented, and a facilities exclusion applies to every trans visitor, so this sits at or just below that anchor.

That anchor has a working traveller-protection statute and legal aid that resolves the gate mismatch in the traveller's favour. Here remedies are injunctions of contested orders, not a working shield, and nothing remedies facility exclusion or custody, so this is materially lower.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is a hostile federal layer applied over a division that is mixed: no current restroom ban and two protective city ordinances, but a 2026 licence and birth-certificate marker ban, a minor care ban, and a pending campus and prison facility bill. For a traveller the sharpest exposures are at the border (marker discrepancy, refusal, possible lifetime ineligibility, reported confiscations and stranding) which feeds into an immigration-custody system with documented beatings, forced labour and sexual abuse, and in federally funded sex-segregated facilities where birth-sex exclusion operates regardless of local tolerance. Hate-crime coverage and litigation give partial, uneven recourse, but courts are also enforcing the hostile document rules, so they do not offset the exposures. A minor travelling with a guardian faces additional outing risk in facilities and a care ban.
